name: AI Assistant Bridge (MCP)
summary: PC only. Lets an AI assistant such as Claude read your lines, vehicles, towns and the vehicles you can buy, to suggest fleet changes. Read-only.
description:
Connects your game to an AI assistant through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), so you can ask things like "which lines lose money?", "which trains are past their lifespan and what should replace them?" or "which big towns have no rail service?".

What the assistant can see:
- lines: stops and their towns, vehicles, capacity usage, 12-month profit, profit per vehicle, running costs and problems
- vehicles: model, age against lifespan, maintenance, current load, running cost, value and profit
- towns: population, size per district, public transport reach and the lines serving them
- vehicle models you can buy this year: price, capacity, top speed, power and lifespan

SETUP (Windows PC only; on consoles the mod switches itself off. Needs Python 3.8+ and an MCP app such as the Claude desktop app or Claude Code):
1. Enable this mod for your save. It can be added to an existing save and removed again.
2. Get the companion MCP server (one Python file, no extra packages) and register it with your AI app by pasting this into PowerShell:
$d="$env:LOCALAPPDATA\tf3-mcp"; mkdir $d -Force >$null; iwr https://github.com/bsaurusrex/tf3-ai-assistant-bridge/releases/latest/download/tf3_mcp_server.py -OutFile "$d\tf3_mcp_server.py"; py "$d\tf3_mcp_server.py" --setup
   It downloads the server from the GitHub release below and registers it with the Claude desktop app and Claude Code.
3. Quit the Claude app from the system tray, reopen it, load your save and ask away.
Full guide, manual download, other MCP apps and troubleshooting: https://github.com/bsaurusrex/tf3-ai-assistant-bridge

How it works: the companion MCP server asks the game for data whenever the assistant needs it, through small files in the game's user data folder, and the mod answers with live numbers. Between requests the mod does nothing. It never changes your game, sends no commands and makes no network connections. Work is spread over frames, so it does not cause stutter, even on large maps.

Settings: CPU time per frame, town list on or off, and logging.
